issues.body: The dispatch branch still emits type=raw,value=${{ needs.setup.outputs.version }}, while setup.outputs.version is the unconstrained required inputs.tag. Thus workflow_dispatch with tag=latest, a stable semver tag, or a moving major.minor tag can still push and overwrite the canonical image tag. This contradicts the comments' load-bearing claim that the trigger paths are disjoint and that a developer/test build can never claim a deployment-followed tag. The added tests do not exercise adversarial input resolution and therefore remain insufficient for this safety property.
issues.fix_hint: Before publishing, reject reserved/canonical dispatch tag forms (at minimum latest, stable semver release tags, and moving major.minor tags), or unconditionally namespace the container tag for dispatch builds, such as dev-<sanitized-version>. Extend scripts/tests/test_release_container_multiarch.py with cases that model latest, stable semver, and major.minor collisions and prove they are rejected or mapped to a noncanonical tag.
issues.title: Manual dispatch can still overwrite canonical container tags

verdict.summary: Round 2 is stagnant: the prior major finding remains unchanged. The new trigger guards suppress the explicit canonical tag entries during workflow_dispatch, but the dispatch-controlled inputs.tag is still copied unchanged through setup.outputs.version into a raw pushed image tag. A caller can therefore dispatch with latest, a stable release version, or a moving major.minor value and overwrite a deployment-followed/canonical tag. The expanded structural tests still assert only the literal YAML tag configuration and mutations; they do not validate or constrain the effective dispatch tag set for colliding inputs.
